claim: Embryogenesis is a multiscale process during which developmental symmetry breaking transitions give rise to complex multicellular organisms.
source: Embryogenesis is a multiscale process during which developmental symmetry breaking transitions give rise to complex multicellular organisms.
evidence: This is a general statement about embryogenesis that draws from established scientific understanding of developmental biology.

claim: Recent advances in high-resolution live-cell microscopy provide unprecedented insights into the collective cell dynamics at various stages of embryonic development.
source: Recent advances in high-resolution live-cell microscopy provide unprecedented insights into the collective cell dynamics at various stages of embryonic development.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent literature on imaging technologies in the Introduction section.

claim: The mode-based model learning framework can translate single-cell trajectory data on curved surfaces into quantitative models for the dominant hydrodynamic modes.
source: Building on these ideas, we construct and demonstrate here a computational framework that translates developmental single-cell trajectory data on curved surfaces into quantitative models for the dominant hydrodynamic modes.
evidence: This is the main methodological contribution demonstrated through the manuscript's results with both synthetic and experimental data.

claim: Mode representations provide a powerful tool to decompose and study system dynamics at and across different energetic, spatial and temporal scales.
source: Widely applied in physics (Kac, 1966; Goldenfeld and Woese, 2011; Kantsler and Goldstein, 2012; Bhaduri et al., 2020), engineering (Soong and Grigoriu, 1993; Heydari et al., 2021), and spectral computing (Driscoll et al., 2014; Burns et al., 2020; Fortunato et al., 2021), mode representations (Schmid, 2010; Tu et al., 2014) provide a powerful tool to decompose and study system dynamics at and across different energetic, spatial and temporal scales.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work in physics, engineering, and spectral computing.

claim: Mode representations are not yet widely used to characterize and compress cell tracking data, or to infer dynamic models from such data.
source: Despite this fact, however, mode representations are not yet widely used to characterize and compress cell tracking data, or to infer dynamic models from such data.
evidence: This is an observation about the current state of the field, based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: The experimentally observed cell motions during early zebrafish gastrulation are approximately two-dimensional.
source: The experimentally observed cell motions are approximately two-dimensional (2D): The radius of the yolk cell surface on which the dynamics takes place is much larger than the average height changes of the evolving cell mass (Shah et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Shah et al., 2019 and is used to justify the 2D approximation in the model.

claim: A thin film approximation is adopted where cellular motion is represented on an effective spherical mid-surface.
source: We therefore adopt a thin film approximation, in which the cellular motion is represented on an effective spherical mid-surface (gray surface in Figure 1B); refined future models should aim to account for the full 3D dynamics.
evidence: This is a methodological choice made by the authors, justified by the 2D nature of the observed cell motions.

claim: Cell divisions are essential to most developmental processes.
source: Because cell divisions are essential to most developmental processes, total cell numbers will in many cases – including early zebrafish gastrulation (Kobitski et al., 2015) – vary over time.
evidence: This is a general biological fact supported by citation to Kobitski et al., 2015 for the specific case of zebrafish gastrulation.

claim: Total cell numbers vary over time during early zebrafish gastrulation.
source: Because cell divisions are essential to most developmental processes, total cell numbers will in many cases – including early zebrafish gastrulation (Kobitski et al., 2015) – vary over time.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kobitski et al., 2015.

claim: The time point at around 300 min approximately marks the completion of epiboly.
source: Interestingly, this time point approximately marks the completion of epiboly, when the different cell layers have fully engulfed the yolk.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data in relation to known developmental stages.

claim: Mode signatures of the symmetry breaking and progression through developmental stages are robust.
source: We find that mode signatures of the symmetry breaking and progression through developmental stages are robust (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, D), illustrating that mode-based analysis can provide a systematic and meaningful characterization of developmental symmetry breaking events.
evidence: This is demonstrated by analyzing a second experimental dataset, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The total topological charge of defects in the cell flux on a sphere always sums to +2.
source: Because the vector-valued flux is defined on a sphere, we observe that the total topological charge always sums to +2 (Kamien, 2002), while additional defect pairs with opposite charge (red +1 and white -1 circles in Figure 2A) can be created, resulting in total defect numbers greater than two (see Figure 2C, bottom).
evidence: This is a topological constraint for vector fields on a sphere, supported by citation to Kamien, 2002, and verified in the data.

claim: Topological defects in the 2D projected cellular flux fields could signal the start of the formation of more complex structures in three dimensions.
source: The appearance of additional defects at the end of epiboly, when the developing embryo begins to extrude more significantly in the radial direction, suggests that topological defects in the 2D projected cellular flux fields could signal the start of the formation of more complex structures in three dimensions.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed correlation between defect formation and developmental stage.

claim: The inference framework correctly recovers the hydrodynamic equations for active Brownian particle (ABP) dynamics on curved surfaces.
source: To validate the approach, we demonstrate that it correctly recovers the hydrodynamic equations for active Brownian particle (ABP) dynamics on curved surfaces.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing the learned matrix M with the analytically predicted matrix for ABP dynamics, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Direct simulation of the learned model for ABP dynamics agrees very well with the dynamics of the coarse-grained input data.
source: Indeed, direct simulation of the learned model projected in real space (Figure 3E) reveals a density and flux dynamics that agrees very well with the dynamics of the the coarse-grained input data (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by visual comparison of Figure 3D and 3E.

claim: The MAD-rescaled matrix learned for the experimental zebrafish data shows similar patterns of prominent diagonal and block-diagonal couplings as the matrix learned for ABP dynamics.
source: Comparing the MAD-rescaled matrix (see Appendix 4) learned for the experimental zebrafish data (Figure 4B) with the non-dimensionalized matrix learned for the active Brownian particle dynamics (Figure 3C), we find similar patterns of prominent diagonal and block-diagonal couplings.
evidence: This is observed by visual comparison of Figure 4B and Figure 3C.

claim: A random, but persistent movement of cells akin to ABPs moving on a sphere partially contributes to the early gastrulation process in zebrafish.
source: Consistent with the analysis of single cell trajectories (Shah et al., 2019), this suggests that a random, but persistent movement of cells akin to ABPs moving on a sphere partially contributes to the early gastrulation process in zebrafish.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity between the learned matrices for zebrafish and ABP dynamics, and is consistent with prior analysis by Shah et al., 2019.

claim: Simulations with modified initial conditions still exhibit a characteristic symmetry breaking and lead to the emergence of density and flux patterns similar to those seen in the original data.
source: Furthermore, simulations with modified initial conditions (see Figure 4—figure supplement 1) still exhibit a characteristic symmetry breaking and lead to the emergence of density and flux patterns similar to those seen in Figure 4F and G.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the simulations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The real-space analysis reveals an effectively non-local coupling between density and flux dynamics in the zebrafish data.
source: In conclusion, the real-space analysis and comparison of inferred interaction kernels further highlights potential ABP-like contributions to the collective cellular organization during early zebrafish development and reveals an effectively non-local coupling between density and flux dynamics.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of the kernel m^ρ(r,r') shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The non-local coupling between density and flux could result from unresolved fast-evolving morphogens, mechanical interactions with the surrounding material, or other relevant degrees of freedom not explicitly captured in the linear hydrodynamic model.
source: The latter could result, for example, from unresolved fast-evolving morphogens (Hannezo and Heisenberg, 2019), through mechanical interactions with the surrounding material (Münster et al., 2019) or due to other relevant degrees of freedom that are not explicitly captured in this linear hydrodynamic model.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed non-local coupling, supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: The learned linear minimal model for cell migration during early zebrafish morphogenesis quantitatively recapitulates the spatiotemporal dynamics of the developmental process.
source: The learned linear minimal model for cell migration during early zebrafish morphogenesis quantitatively recapitulates the spatiotemporal dynamics of a complex developmental process (Figure 4F and G), and highlights similarities between collective cell migration and analytically tractable ABP dynamics on a curved surface.
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing the model predictions with experimental data in Figure 4F and G.

claim: The learned model highlights similarities between collective cell migration during early zebrafish morphogenesis and analytically tractable ABP dynamics on a curved surface.
source: The learned linear minimal model for cell migration during early zebrafish morphogenesis quantitatively recapitulates the spatiotemporal dynamics of a complex developmental process (Figure 4F and G), and highlights similarities between collective cell migration and analytically tractable ABP dynamics on a curved surface.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of the learned matrices and kernels for zebrafish and ABP dynamics.

claim: An extension to nonlinear mode-coupling models or an integration of additional experimentally measured degrees of freedom is in principle straightforward by including nonlinear terms in Equation 12.
source: An extension to nonlinear mode-coupling models or an integration of additional, experimentally measured degrees of freedom, such as concentration fields of morphogens involved in mechanochemical feedbacks (Hannezo and Heisenberg, 2019), is in principle straightforward by including nonlinear terms in Equation 12.
evidence: This is a statement about potential future extensions of the framework.

claim: The framework could be generalized to describe the dynamics within a spherical shell of finite height by complementing the surface vector SHs with their radial counterpart.
source: Furthermore, the above framework could be generalized to describe the dynamics within a spherical shell of finite height by complementing the surface vector SHs used in this work by their radial counterpart (Barrera et al., 1985).
evidence: This is a statement about potential future extensions of the framework, supported by citation to Barrera et al., 1985.

claim: The essentially spherical organization of cells during gastrulation observed in zebrafish is shared by many species whose early development occurs through discoidal cleavage.
source: However, the essentially spherical organization of cells during gastrulation observed in zebrafish is shared by many species whose early development occurs through a similar discoidal cleavage (Gilbert and Barresi, 2016), and the framework introduced here is directly applicable once tracking data becomes available for these systems.
evidence: This is a statement about the generalizability of the approach, supported by citation to Gilbert and Barresi, 2016.

claim: The framework is directly applicable to other species with similar spherical organization of cells during gastrulation once tracking data becomes available.
source: However, the essentially spherical organization of cells during gastrulation observed in zebrafish is shared by many species whose early development occurs through a similar discoidal cleavage (Gilbert and Barresi, 2016), and the framework introduced here is directly applicable once tracking data becomes available for these systems.
evidence: This is a statement about the applicability of the framework to other biological systems.

claim: Two single-cell tracking data sets were obtained from the experiments described in Shah et al., 2019.
source: We obtained two single-cell tracking data sets from the experiments described in Shah et al., 2019.
evidence: This describes the source of the experimental data used in the study.

claim: Some of the data is accessible at https://idr.openmicroscopy.org with ID number idr0068.
source: Some of the data is accessible at https://idr.openmicroscopy.org with ID number idr0068.
evidence: This provides information about data availability.

claim: Cell trajectories were denoised using MATLAB's wavelet denoiser function wdenoise.
source: We first denoised each cell trajectory using MATLAB's (Matlab, 2019) wavelet denoiser function wdenoise, and centered the cloud of cells by least-squares fitting a spherical surface through it and shifting the origin at each time to coincide with the center of this sphere.
evidence: This describes a specific data processing step.

claim: Cell velocities were computed using Tikhonov-regularized differentiation as described in Knowles and Renka, 2014.
source: We then computed the velocity of each cell by using Tikhonov-regularized differentiation as described in Knowles and Renka, 2014 and implemented in the MATLAB third-party module rdiff (Wagner, 2020).
evidence: This describes a specific data processing step, supported by citations.

claim: Outlier cells whose speed is in the 95th percentile or above were removed.
source: After examination of the cells' velocity distribution, we further removed outlier cells whose speed is in the 95th percentile or above and verified that this operation only removes aberrant cells.
evidence: This describes a specific data filtering step.
